**For overnight cooks, I’d choose the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2.** Its 2,073.6 Wh capacity and 2,600 W inverter give plenty of headroom for a pellet smoker’s ignition surge, and the cited estimate is **two or three 12-hour cooks per charge**. [See the product details and availability](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-pellet-smoker-overnight) or [buy the Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2).

A pellet smoker typically draws only about **35–60 W once it’s running**, but uses more power briefly to ignite. The same guide estimates **450–750 Wh for a 12-hour cook**, so a roughly 1 kWh station may cover one overnight cook; extra campsite devices will cut into that runtime. Check your smoker’s startup draw against the station’s inverter rating, and keep the station dry and away from grill heat. ([Sizing and runtime details](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-pellet-smoker-overnight))

*This advice is for a pellet smoker/grill, not an electric smoker with a heating element, which needs much more power.*
